newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES THRIVES AS TEAM PLAYER IN FED CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES THRIVES AS TEAM PLAYER IN FED CUP WIN.

text.p: The United States needed a big gun to end Spain's reign as Fed Cup champions and Monica Seles provided the necessary firepower.

A great champion in the egocentric world of big-time tennis, Seles thrived in the unique Fed Cup team atmosphere, leading her adopted country to a 5-0 victory over Spain in the final on Saturday and Sunday.
Three times in the past five years the United States had reached the final only to be thwarted by Spain's Barcelona bashers, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Conchita Martinez.

This year Seles rode to the rescue, with her two-fisted groundstrokes blazing. She won the opening and championship-clinching matches, raising her career record over the Spanish duo to a combined 23-1.
"Two years ago the women said we've got to get Monica to play when she comes back," U.S. captain Billie Jean King recalled.
"I said that means one of you may not be on the team and they said 'We don't care, we want to bring back the Cup to the United States'
"It's wonderful that they feel that strongly about it and (Seles) certainly has changed the equasion," said King, a member of the inaugural Federation Cup champion team of 1963.

Something of a loner earlier in her career, Seles was downright rattled by the fear of letting her new friends down. It added a tension she said she had not experienced in major matches before and a potential payoff of comrades to share her joy.
"It's very different ... having your teammates behind you cheering you on," she said.
"This means so much to me because it's the first time I've done anything on a team.

"When I first got to Nagoya (for the semifinals) I wasn't sure what to expect because I've never been on a team. And my whole summer I've loved it and to finish it off by winning the Fed Cup, which we haven't won since 1990, is like the ideal ending," Seles said.

"I could tell after one minute that she was going to be a great team player," said King of her initial Fed Cup encounter with the superstar. "She was just so positive from the first moment. No nonsense I call her, she's just no nonsense."
"Monica is focused on every single ball, every single day.

"She knew what she had to do and she just went out and did it. She's totally driven, that's why she's such a great champion," added King, putting Seles in a class with Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Steffi Graf.
King said there was an added bonus to having Seles around besides the two points she virtually guarantees the team in most any best-of-five tie.
Seles's extreme intensity had rubbed off on Lindsay Davenport, helping spur her to an inspired victory over Sanchez on Saturday that gave the Americans a 2-0 lead going into the final day.
"It has made a difference for Lindsay being around Monica. If you saw Lindsay practice a year ago compared to now you wouldn't believe the difference," King said.
Davenport admitted to being pleasantly surprised by Seles's selflessness in practice.
And she and Cup veteran Mary Joe Fernandez were touched by how much Seles seemed to want to help them win after years of falling just short.
"She has been such a great team player," Davenport said.
"She was really nervous, she told us, for these two matches. I think she really wanted to win it for us also, which is really nice," Davenport said.

In a building famous for hosting the Miss America pageant, Monica Seles, born in Yugoslavia to parents of Hugarian descent, became Miss USA on Sunday -- at least as far as her captain and teammates are concerned.
"All of us are very psyched that it's back in the States," Seles said.
"We should try to do it again next year."
